Admission needs a legal entity. The applicant submits an OV code-signing certificate, the node walks the CA chain to the root, reads the organisation number against the state business register, then demands an annual filing to keep the seat past twelve months. One company backs one key, rechecked at renewal.

An anchor bites only the ground under it, and a firm at its nadir still owes filings. Fifty clones need fifty incorporated firms: 300 dollars to register, 900 a year in agent and filing fees, 350 for CA vetting, near 60,000 dollars before one umber stamp lands on a page.
